note: Measured with `NO_COLOR=1 bash bin/crossrev <args>` in a checkout. shell is what the shell printed on stderr and the status it ended with, with any absolute checkout path replaced by <checkout>; native is what this package prints where it cannot reproduce the shell byte for byte, with the reason recorded beside it. A row with no native block must match its shell block exactly. Every row printed nothing on stdout.
on the bash frames: A shell block reading `<checkout>/lib/<file>.sh: line N: 2: ...` is a `${2:?...}` refusal, which Bash prints itself. Those blocks are a record of what the shell did and never a contract: the row carries a native block, so the test compares against that and nothing reads the shell bytes. N moves with any edit above it in the library file, and it has gone stale twice already. Re-measure it when you touch the file rather than trusting it, and never derive one number from another by adding an offset.
